description: Common feature engineering patterns and date/text decomposition strategies

date_decomposition.name: Date Column Decomposition
date_decomposition.explanation: Raw dates are unusable by ML models. Decomposing into components captures seasonality, day-of-week effects, and trends.
date_decomposition.business_impact: Date decomposition reveals seasonal patterns (Q4 holiday spikes), day-of-week effects (Monday dips), and long-term trends invisible in raw date format.
date_decomposition.example: Decomposed 'order_date' into year, month, day_of_week, quarter, is_weekend — enabling seasonal analysis and day-of-week demand patterns.

date_decomposition.name: Time Duration Features
date_decomposition.condition: Two date columns exist (start/end pattern detected)
date_decomposition.explanation: The difference between two dates often contains more predictive power than the dates themselves (e.g., length of stay, delivery time, tenure).
date_decomposition.example: Created 'tenure_days' from 'hire_date' to 'current_date' — tenure is a stronger predictor of attrition than raw hire date.

text_handling.name: Text Length Feature
text_handling.explanation: Text length can be a useful feature (longer product descriptions may correlate with different sales patterns).
text_handling.example: Created 'description_length' from 'product_description' — longer descriptions correlate with 12% higher conversion rates.

text_handling.name: Text Category Extraction
text_handling.condition: Column contains semi-structured text with extractable categories
text_handling.explanation: Extract structured features from semi-structured text using regex or keyword matching.
text_handling.example: Extracted 'has_discount_mention' from 'product_title' — products with 'sale' or 'discount' in title have 2.3× click rate.

numeric_combinations.name: Ratio Features
numeric_combinations.condition: Two related numeric columns exist (e.g., revenue and quantity, or cost and price)
numeric_combinations.explanation: Ratios normalize for scale and often reveal efficiency or profitability patterns invisible in raw values.
numeric_combinations.example: Created 'revenue_per_unit' from 'total_revenue / quantity' — reveals pricing efficiency across product categories.

numeric_combinations.name: Binning / Discretization
numeric_combinations.condition: Continuous numeric column with clear business-meaningful ranges
numeric_combinations.explanation: Converting continuous values to bins (Low/Medium/High or age groups) can reveal non-linear relationships and improve interpretability.
numeric_combinations.example: Binned 'age' into groups (18-25, 26-35, 36-50, 51+) — reveals that the 26-35 age group has 40% higher purchase frequency.

aggregation_features.name: Group-Level Statistics
aggregation_features.condition: Dataset has a natural grouping column (customer_id, department, region)
aggregation_features.explanation: Rolling up individual records to group-level statistics captures entity behavior patterns (high-spending customers, high-performing departments).
aggregation_features.example: Created 'customer_avg_order_value' by grouping on 'customer_id' — this feature captures individual customer spending patterns.

column_dropping_rules.name: Constant Column
column_dropping_rules.explanation: A column with zero variance provides no information for analysis or modeling.

column_dropping_rules.name: Near-Zero Variance
column_dropping_rules.explanation: Near-constant columns add noise without signal. Verify the rare values aren't meaningful before dropping.

column_dropping_rules.name: High Cardinality ID-like
column_dropping_rules.condition: Column has unique values equal to row count AND appears to be an identifier
column_dropping_rules.explanation: ID columns have no predictive power and cause models to memorize individual records (overfitting). Keep for reference but exclude from feature sets.

column_dropping_rules.name: Highly Correlated Redundant
column_dropping_rules.explanation: Near-perfect correlation means the columns carry the same information. Keep the more interpretable/complete one.
